name: Respond (CFTR) API Reference
description:
Cyware Fusion and Threat Response (CFTR) is a threat response automation platform that combines cyber fusion, advanced orchestration, and automation. Using the CFTR application security analysts can tackle all kinds of threats including malware, vulnerabilities, incidents, campaigns, and threat actors. Using the CFTR integrated threat databases, security analysts can manage and respond to all kinds of security threats such as malware, vulnerabilities, and threat actors.

CFTR API is organized around REST. You can use this API Reference to engage with the CFTR services programmatically and enable any automation or integration with other systems in your environment.

Note: You can make a maximum of 6000 API requests every 15 minutes to Respond.

Supported Version

Cyware Fusion and Threat Response (CFTR) v3.0 and higher.

Note: You can download the Postman API collection and Swagger API collection using the following links:

  • Postman Collection

  • Swagger Collection

endpoints.name: Test connectivity
endpoints.description:
Test the connectivity with the CFTR platform.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response

The API response status is 200 (OK) if all the following parameters are correct:

  1. Base URL
  2. URL Path
  3. Access ID
  4. Signature
  5. Expires

responses.schema: "Success"

examples.name: Test connectivity
examples.response: "Success"

endpoints.name: Get Incident Workflows Listing
endpoints.description:
Retrieve a list of all the incident workflows with details from your CFTR application.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Each incident workflow detail in the response contains the following parameters:

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the Incident Workflow.
description String Description of the Incident Workflow.
unique_id String Unique Identifier String of UUID-4 format of the Incident Worflow.
schema_type String Defines the state of Incident Workflow as `draft` OR `published`.
status String Describes the state of Incident Workflow as `active` or `inactive`.
is_default Boolean Determines whether the Incident Workflow is the default one or not.
object_identifier String Determines the string name for Incident Module.
phase_flow String Determines the selected flow of Workflow phases as `linear` or `non-linear`.
created String Timestamp String in ISO Format describing the date-time of creation of the Incident Workflow.
modified String Timestamp String in ISO Format describing the date-time of latest modification of the Incident Workflow.
created_by String user_id in UUID-4 format of the user who created the Incident Workflow.
modified_by String user_id in UUID-4 format of the User who lastly modified the Incident Workflow.
created_by_data Object Basic details of the user who created the Incident Workflow.
modified_by_data Object Basic details of the user who lastly modified the Incident Workflow.
is_removed Boolean Determines whether the Workflow is in deleted state or not.
is_mapped Boolean Determines whether the Incident Workflow has been mapped to parent parameters or not.
num_of_phases Integer Determines the number of phases present in the Incident Workflow.
is_imported Boolean Determines if the Workflow is imported or not.

endpoints.name: List Incident Workflow Fields
endpoints.description:
Get Incident Types

Retrieve details of the Fields present in Form Management module of the Respond.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
results array Returns the list of fields added in the Form Management.
unique_id string Returns the unique identifier of the incident.
field_name string Returns the name of the incident form field. For example, Incident Type
field_type string Enter the type for the field
For example, select to indicate a dropdown.
is_active boolean Indicates whether this field is currently active.
is_removed boolean Indicates whether this field was deleted or not.
order integer Returns the position of the field in the incident form layout.
placeholder string Returns the placeholder text shown when no option is selected.
help_text string Returns the tooltip text of the field.
field_options array Returns the list of selectable options.
is_editable boolean Indicates whether this field configuration can be edited.
is_deletable boolean Indicates whether this field can be deleted from the configuration.
is_table_column boolean Indicates whether this field is shown as a column in the listing page.
is_required boolean Indicates whether this field is mandatory when submitting the form.
is_required_for_creation boolean Indicates whether a value is mandatory only when creating a new incident.
type string Returns the type of the field.
prepopulator_value string or null Returns any default value configured for this field.
field_readable_key string Returns the key used to uniquely identify this field. For example, ie_incident_type
is_widget_field boolean Indicates whether this field is available as a widget element in the UI.
extra_params object Returns the other details of the field.
data_source string Returns data source for populating this field.
dependent_options_data array Returns the configurations for options that depend on other field values.
always_visible boolean Indicates whether this field is always visible, regardless of conditions.
column_no integer Column index where the field appears in multi-column layouts.
is_read_only boolean Indicates whether the field is read-only.
is_sla_field boolean Indicates whether this field is related to SLA.
enable_filter boolean Indicates whether this field can be used as a filter in search.
is_restricted_user_group_write_access boolean Indicates if write access to this field is restricted to specific user groups.
user_groups_with_write_access array Returns the IDs of user groups that have write access to this field.
is_restricted boolean Indicates whether access to this field is restricted to specific user or user groups.
user_groups_with_write_access_data array Returns the detailed metadata for user groups that have write access.
is_parent_param boolean Indicates whether this field acts as a parent parameter for dependent fields.
is_field_new boolean Indicates whether this field is newly added in the form.
note_mandatory boolean Indicates whether adding a note is mandatory when modifying this field.
editable_fields array Returns the list of sub fields that can be edited for this field.
is_enabled boolean Indicates whether this field is enabled and available in the UI.
editable_readable_key boolean Indicates whether the field's readable key can be edited.
process_intel_automatically boolean Indicates whether intelligence processing is automatically enabled for this field.
process_intel_cftr_enable boolean Indicates whether Respond-specific intelligence processing is enabled for this field.
process_intel_ctix_enable boolean Indicates whether CTIX-specific threat intelligence processing is enabled for this field.
is_dynamic_column boolean Indicates whether this field is treated as a dynamic column in tabular views.

endpoints.name: Get Incident Workflow Details
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of an incident workflow.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Each incident workflow detail in the response contains the following parameters:

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the Incident Workflow.
description String Description of the Incident Workflow.
unique_id String Unique ID of the Incident Workflow.
schema_type String Shows the state of Incident Workflow.
Allowed values:
- draft
- published
status String Status of the Incident Workflow.
Allowed values:
- active
- inactive
is_default Boolean Shows whether the Incident Workflow is the default workflow or not.
object_identifier String Shows the string name for Incident module.
phase_flow String Shows the phase flow of the Incident Workflow phases.
Allowed values:
- linear
- non-linear
created String Creation date-time of the Incident Workflow.
modified String Latest modification date-time of the Incident Workflow.
created_by String user_id of the user who created the Incident Workflow.
modified_by String user_id of the user who last modified the Incident Workflow.
created_by_data Object Basic details of user who created the Incident Workflow.
modified_by_data Object Basic details of the user who last modified the Incident Workflow.
is_removed Boolean Shows whether the workflow is in deleted state or not.
is_mapped Boolean Shows whether the Incident Workflow has been mapped to parent parameters or not.
num_of_phases Integer Number of phases present in the Incident Workflow.
closure_phase String unique_id of phase after which incident can be closed.
closure_phase_data Object Details of the closure phase.
Details include: option_name, unique_id, and so on.
phase_key String unique_id of the phases.
preparation_key String unique_id of the preparation tab.
custom_tab_key String unique_id of the custom tabs.
closure_phase_options Array unique_id of all the phases of the Incident Workflow which can be selected as the closure phase.
tabs Array unique_id of the tabs of the Incident Workflow.
Response Parameters | Form Tab Structure
Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the Tab.
tab_name String Title of the tab.
is_active Boolean Shows if the tab is active or not.
is_editable Boolean Shows if the tab can be edited or not.
is_removed Boolean Shows whether the tab is in deleted state or not.
object_identifier String Shows the string name for Incident module
tab_fields List of Objects Details of the fields added in the tab.
Note: The tab fields are further explained in the table below.
tab_type String The tab type.
Examples of tab types are:
preparation: Preparation tab is common across all workflows.
phase: Phase
custom: Custom Tab
parent String unique_id of the parent of the tab.
children List Details of children tabs.
is_removable Boolean Shows if tab can be removed or not.
validation_expression String Validation expression (if any) added. It is used for Threat Intel.
schema List List of unique_id of workflows in which the tab is added.
order Integer Order of the tab.
help_text String Help text of the tab
Response Parameters | Tab Fields Structure
Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique identifier string of UUID-4 format of the Field.
field_name String Title of the field.
field_type String The type of field.
Allowed values:
select: Single option can be selected for the field.
multiselect: Multiple options can be selected for the field.
text: Text field.
textarea: Text Area field.
calendar: date time field.

Applicable only for select/multi-select fields.

endpoints.name: Get List of OS Types
endpoints.description:
Retrieve a list of all OS types with details from the CFTR application.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Total number of OS types in CFTR application according to the filters applied.

endpoints.name: Get details of one User
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of a user from your CFTR application.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
user_id String Unique ID of the user in UUID-4 format.
permission List of String The list of permissions configured for the user in the CFTR application.
Note: The permissions depend on the user groups of the user.
last_login String Last log in date and time of the user in ISO Format.
first_name String First name of the user.
last_name String Last name of the user.
email String Email ID of the user.
title String Job title of the user.
display_pic String The link to the display picture of the user.
groups List of String List of unique IDs of group_comm_id of the User Groups in UUID-4 format.
groups_data List of Objects Details of the User Groups. Each object includes the details of one User Group such as group_comm_id, group_name, and description.
country_code String Country code of the user.
contact_number String Contact number of the user.
username String Username of the user.
location String Unique ID of the location of the user in UUID-4 format.
location_data Object Details of the user location.
allowed_locations List of Strings List of unique IDs of the allowed locations of the user in UUID-4 format.
allowed_locations_data List of Objects Details of the allowed locations of the user. Each object includes the details of one location.
Details include:
title, unique_id, and is_active.
business_unit String Unique ID of the Business Unit of the user in UUID-4 format.
business_unit_data Object Details of the Business Unit of the user.
allowed_business_units List of Strings List of unique IDs of the allowed Business Units of the user in UUID-4 format.
allowed_business_units_data List of Objects Details of the allowed Business Units of the user. Each object includes the details of one Business Unit.
Details include:
title, description, unique_id, created,and so on
is_active Boolean Shows whether the user is an active user or not.
date_joined Datetime Joining date and time of the user in ISO format.
is_onboarded Boolean Shows whether the user has activated their account using the confirmation link or not.
date_onboarded String Onboarding date and time of the user in ISO format.
is_bot Boolean Shows whether the user is a bot user or not.
is_admin Boolean Shows whether the user is an admin in the CFTR application or not.
show_related_incidents Boolean Shows whether the user has access to view related incidents in the Connect The Dots section or not.
show_related_assets Boolean Shows if the user has access to view the related assets in Connect the Dots or not.
show_briefings_escalation Boolean Shows if the user has access to view briefings escalations.
date_onboarded String Date and time of when the user was onboarded.
landing_component String Unique ID of the landing component configured for the user in UUID-4 format.
landing_component_data Object Details of the landing component configured for the user.
allowed_components List of Objects Details of the allowed components of the user. Each object includes the details of one component.
Details include:
component_comm_id, component_name, code_name, and component_identifier.
last_active String Last active date and time of the user in ISO format.
last_device String Details of the last device used by the user.
last_device_ip String Generic IP address of the device last used by the user.
currency String Currency choice associated with the user.
Allowed values: INR, USD, GBP, EUR, andAED.
invited_by String Unique ID of the user who invited the current user.
ldap_id String Unique ID of LDAP associated with the user.
full_name String Full name of the user.
password_update_time String Last updated date and time of the password of the user in ISO format.
analyst_cost Float Maximum value of analyst cost associated with each user group of the user.
is_system_user Boolean Shows whether the user is a system user or not.
invite_status String Shows whether the user has accepted the invite or not.
Allowed values:
- INVITED: Invite yet to be accepted.
- ACCEPTED: Invite accepted.
is_on_prem_client Boolean Displays if the user is a on prem client.
is_readonly_user Boolean If the user is has only ready-only access.
number_of_incidents_per_day Integer The number of incidents that can be created by the user.
number_of_business_units Integer Number of business units

Note: The permissions of a user depend on the User Groups of the user. If a user is assigned to more than User Groups, then the permissions of all the User Groups apply for the user.

Response Parameters | Location and Allowed Locations Data Objects

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the location
unique_id String Unique ID of the location in UUID-4 format.
is_active Boolean Shows if the location is active or not.

Response Parameters | Business Unit and Allowed Business Units Data Objects

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the Business Unit.
description Text Description of the Business Unit.
unique_id String Unique ID of the Business Unit in UUID-4 format.
created String Creation date and time of the Business Unit in ISO format.
modified String Last modified date and time of the Business Unit in ISO format.
readable_id String Unique readable ID of the Business Unit. It starts with BU followed by a unique number
Example: "BU101"

Response Parameters | Groups Data Object

Parameter Type Description
group_comm_id String Unique ID of the User Group in UUID-4 format.
group_name String Name of the User Group.
description Text Description of the User Group.

Response Parameters | Allowed Components and Landing Component Data Objects

Parameter Type Description
component_comm_id String Unique ID of the component in UUID-4 format.
component_name String Name of the component.
code_name String Code name of the component.
component_identifier String Identification string of the component.

Example Error Codes

Error Code Description
500 User with the given unique ID does not exist.

results List of Objects Details of the User Groups.

endpoints.name: Get List of Incidents
endpoints.description:
Retrieve a list of all the incidents with details from the CFTR application.

You can use the single-select and multi-select fields as query parameters to filter incidents.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/incident/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Total number of incidents in CFTR application according to the filters applied.
results List of Objects Details of the incidents.
Each object provides details of one incident.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the Incident in UUID-4 format.
readable_id String Unique readable ID of the incident. It starts with INC followed by a unique number.
Example: INC101
created String Incident creation date and time.
description Text Description of the Incident.
modified String Last updated date and time of the incident.
title Text Title of the incident.
machine_generated Boolean True: Incident is considered machine generated when it is generated using the CFTR OpenAPI.
False: Incident created manually.
status String Current status of the incident.
Allowed values:
open
closed
untriaged
merged
closed_on String Date and time when the incident was closed.
If incident is not closed, value of this param will be Null.
title_display String Title of the incident.
is_protected Boolean Shows if the incident is marked as protected or not.
level String Severity level of the incident.
phase String Current phase of the incident.
is_paused Boolean Shows if the incident is paused or not.
opened_on String Date and time when the incident was opened.
If incident is not opened yet, value of this param will be Null.
assignment_sla Object Assignment SLA details of the incident.
It has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
resolution_sla Object Resolution SLA details of the incident.
It has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows if the incident is bookmarked or not.
resolution_due_date Datetime Resolution SLA breach date of the incident.
opened_by_data Object Details of the user who opened the incident. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
parent_data Object If Incident is merged to an incident, this parameter contains details of the parent incident. Details include:
title, unique_id, and readable_id.
modified_by_data Object Details of user who last updated the Incident. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group. Details include:
group name and group ID.
created_by_data Object Details of user who created the incident. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
assigned_to_data Object Details of the assigned user. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
labels_data List of Objects Details of labels added to the incident. Details include:
title, unique_id, color_code, and so on.
business_units_impacted_data Object Details of business unit impacted by the incident. Details include:
title and unique_id of the business unit.
locations_impacted_data List of Objects Details of locations impacted by the incident. Details include:
title and unique_id.
phase_data Object Details of the current phase of the incident. Details include:
option_name: The name of phase
unique_id: Unique ID of the phase
ie_incident_type_data Object Details of the incident type associated with the incident. Details include:
option_name, unique_id, and so on.
ie_incident_type String Incident type associated with the incident.
level_data Object Details of severity level associated with the incident. Details include:
option_name, unique_id, and so on.

endpoints.name: List Incidents (Advanced)
endpoints.description:
List Incidents Advanced

Retrieves the list of incidents with additional details from the Respond application.

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter (key) Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count number Returns the total number of incidents that match the query across all pages.
results array of objects Returns a list of incident objects for the current page, each object representing a single incident with details.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter (key) Type Description
unique_id string Returns the unique ID of the Incident in UUID-4 format.
readable_id string Returns the unique readable ID of the incident. It starts with INC followed by a unique number.
Example: INC101
title string Returns the title of the incident.
description string Returns the description of the incident.
status string Returns the current status of the incident. For example, Open, Closed
phase string Returns the Current phase of the incident
For example, Containment, Closure
level string Returns the severity level of the incident. For example, Low, Medium, High
incident_date string Returns the Date and time when the incident occurred.
detection_date string Returns the date and time when the incident was detected by the system or analysts.
created string Returns the timestamp when the incident was created.
modified string Returns the timestamp when the incident was last updated.
opened_on string (ISO 8601) Returns the timestamp when the incident was opened for investigation.
closed_on string Returns the timestamp when the incident was closed.
title_display String Title of the incident.
machine_generated boolean True: Incident is considered machine generated when it is generated using the Respond OpenAPI.
False: Incident created manually.
is_protected boolean Returns if the incident is marked as protected or not.
is_paused boolean Returns whether the incident is currently paused or not.
assignment_sla Object Assignment SLA details of the incident.
It has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
resolution_sla Object Resolution SLA details of the incident.
It has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
is_ctix_generated Boolean Returns if the incident was created from Intel Exchange.
is_bookmarked Boolean Returns if the incident is bookmarked.
incident_state string High-level lifecycle state of the incident (often aligned with status, such as Open or Closed).
business_impact array of strings List of business impact labels associated with the incident (for example, Branding Impact).
business_impact_data array of objects Detailed metadata objects for each business impact entry, including ids, names and configuration details.
attack_vector string, not mandatory Primary attack vector associated with the incident (for example, Email), if specified.
attack_vector_data object, not mandatory Metadata describing the selected attack vector option (id, name, status and configuration fields).
ie_incident_type string Classification of the incident type (for example, Malware).
ie_incident_type_data object Metadata describing the selected incident type option (id, name and related configuration info).
opened_by_data object User details for the account that opened the incident (user id, name, email and related attributes).
created_by_data object User details for the account that originally created the incident record.
modified_by_data object User details for the account that last modified the incident.
assigned_group_data object Details of the group or team currently assigned to work on the incident.
assigned_to_data object Details of the individual user currently assigned to handle the incident.
sources_data object Returns the details of the source that generated the incident. Details include: unique_id, source_type, value, and more.
labels_data array of objects Details of labels added to the incident. Details include:
title, unique_id, color_code, and more.
business_units_impacted_data object Returns details of the business units impacted by the incident. Details include:
title and unique_id of the business unit.
locations_impacted_data array of objects Returns the locations impacted by the incident.
first_assigned_on String Returns when the incident was first assigned to a user.
paused_on String Returns the date and time when the incident was paused.
phase_data object Returns the details describing the incident’s current phase (id, display name, order and properties).
status_data object Returns the details describing the incident’s current status.
Details include: id, display name, order and color code
level_data Object Returns the details of severity level associated with the incident. Details include:
option_name, unique_id, and so on.
ie_customer_notification_required_data Object Returns the the details if the the customer notifications for the incident is enabled.

Retrieve the details of an incident.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/incident/:incident_unique_id/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

You can retrieve the details of an incident using the following API endpoint:

{{base-url}}/openapi/v1/forms/incident/schema/{{workflow-unique-id}}/

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the incident.
unique_id String Unique Identifier String of UUID-4 format of the incident.
readable_id String Readable ID of the incident. For example, INC320.
incident_date String Date and time of when the incident happened.
detection_date String Date and time when the incident was detected as malicious.
status String Status of the incident workflow.
Allowed values:
- active
- inactive
phase String Current phase of the incident. The phase describes the UUID of phase, part of the Incident Workflow.
machine_generated Boolean Displays if the incident is machine generated or not.
phase_data Object Details of the current phase of the incident.
level String Severity level of the incident. For example, high.
level_data Object Details of the severity level of the incident.
created_by String user_id of the user who created the incident.
is_protected Boolean Shows if the incident is protected or not.
is_removed Boolean Shows if the incident is in the deleted state or not.
created_by_data Object Details of user who created the incident.
modified_by_data Object Details of the user who last modified the incident.
closed_by_data Object Details of used who closed the incident.
created String Incident creation date and time.
modified String Last updated date and time of the incident.
Opened_on Datetime Date and time when the incident was opened.
closed_on Datetime Date and time when the incident was closed.
If incident is not closed, value of this param will be Null.
ie_num_of_pii_exposed Integer Number of PIRs that were exposed in the incident.
description String Description of the Incident.
assigned_to String user_id of the assigned user.
assigned_to_data Object Details of the assigned user.
assigned_group String group_comm_id of the assigned user group.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group.
assignment_sla String Assignment SLA details of the incident.

It has two keys:

1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).

2. data: It has two keys:

- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.

- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
ie_incident_type Strings The type of incident.
Example, hacking.
days_open Integer Number of days the incident is open.
resolution_sla String Resolution SLA details of the incident.

It has two keys:

1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).

2. data: It has two keys:

- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.

- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
notification_sla String Details of the Incident notifications (if enabled in admin).
total_cost Integer Total cost incurred due to the incident.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows if the incident is bookmarked or not.
permanently_closed Boolean Shows if the incident is permanently closed or not.

endpoints.description:
Create incidents in your CFTR application using the UUID of locations, business units, sources, assigned groups, and assigned users.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/incident/?

Request Parameters

Note:

  • The default value of all the optional parameters is None, if the default value is not mentioned.

  • To create an Untriaged incident, title is mandatory and all the other fields are optional.

  • To create an incident in Open status, title, business_units_impacted, locations_impacted, and assigned_group fields are mandatory.

Parameters Type Required Description
title string Mandatory Enter a title for the incident.
description string Optional Enter a description that best describes the key details of the incident.
status string Optional Enter the status of the incident.
Allowed values:

* untriaged
* open
* closed
* merged

Example:
"untriaged"

Default value: "open"
phase String Optional
Note: By
default, the
incident
phase will be
the initial
phase of the
Incident
Workflow as configured by your CFTR admin.		 Enter the phase of the
incident.
Sample phases:
• Detection Analysis
• Containment
• Investigation and Eradication
• Recovery
• Closure

Example:
“Detection Analysis”
ie_incident_type String Optional Enter the type of the Incident.
Some of the examples Incident Types are:
• Malware
• Phishing
• Spearphishing

Example:
“Malware”
business_units_impacted Array Mandatory Enter the unique IDs of the impacted
Business Units.

available Business Units and their
Unique IDs using the following API
endpoint:
/openapi/v1/utils/business-unit/

sources String Optional Enter the unique ID of the Sources.

following API endpoint:

incident_date datetime Optional Enter the date of occurrence of the incident.
detection_date datetime Optional Enter the incident detection date.
level String Optional Enter the severity level of the
incident.
Some of the example Severity
Levels are:
• Critical
• High
• Medium
• Low

Example:
“Critical”

endpoints.name: Create Incident Using Field Values
endpoints.description:
Creates an incident in your CFTR application by using the field values of locations, business units, sources, assigned groups, and the email IDs of the user you want to assign the incident.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/incident/?

Request Parameters

Notes:

  • If the default value is not mentioned, then the default value of all the optional parameters is None.

  • To create an Untriaged incident, title is mandatory and all the other parameters are optional.

  • To create an incident in Open status, title, business_units_impacted, locations_impacted, and assigned_group are mandatory.

Parameters Type Required Description
title String Mandatory Enter a title for the incident.
description String Optional Enter a description that best describes the key details of the incident.
status String Optional Enter the status of the incident.

Allowed values:
* untriaged
* open
* closed
* merged

Example:
"untriaged"

Default value: "open"
phase String Optional
Note: By
default, the
incident
phase will be
the initial
phase of the
Incident
Workflow as configured by your CFTR admin.		 Enter the phase of the
incident.
Sample phases:
• Detection Analysis
• Containment
• Investigation and Eradication
• Recovery
• Closure

Example:
“Detection Analysis”
ie_incident_type String Optional Enter the type of Incident.
Some examples of Incident Types are:
• Malware
• Phishing
• Spearphishing

Example:
“Malware”
business_units_impacted Array Mandatory Enter the titles of the impacted
business units.
You can retrieve the list of
available Business Units and their
titles using the following API
endpoint:
/openapi/v1/utils/business-unit/

Note: You can add one or more business units impacted, depending on the settings configured in Admin Panel > Configurations > Incident > Other Settings.
locations_impacted Array Mandatory Enter the title of the impacted
locations. You can retrieve the list of
available locations and their titles
using the following API endpoint:
/openapi/v1/utils/location/
sources String Optional Enter the title of the sources.
You can retrieve the list of all available
sources and their titles using the
following API endpoint:
/openapi/v1/utils/source/
incident_date String Optional Enter the date of occurrence of the incident in EPOCH time format.
detection_date String Optional Enter the incident detection date in EPOCH time format.
level String Optional Enter the severity level of the
incident.
Some of the example Severity
Levels are:
• Critical
• High
• Medium
• Low

Example:
“Critical”
assigned_group String Mandatory Enter the title of the user group to assign the incident. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of
User Groups:
/openapi/v1/rest-auth/permission/group/
assigned_to String Optional Enter the email ID of the user to assign the incident. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of
User:
/openapi/v1/rest-auth/user/
labels Array Optional Enter the name of labels to be added to the incident. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of Labels:
/openapi/v1/utils/label/

Response Parameters

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the incident.
description Text Description of the incident.
unique_id String Unique ID of the incident.
readable_id String Unique readable ID of the incident. It starts with INC followed by a unique number.
Example: INC101
status String Current status of the incident.
Allowed values:
open
closed
untriaged
merged
phase String Current phase of the incident. The phase describes the UUID of phase, part of the Incident Workflow.
phase_data Object Details of the current phase of the incident.
level String Severit level of the incident.
level_data Object Details of the severity level of the incident.
created_by String user_id of the user who created the incident.
created_by_data Object Details of user who created the incident.
modified_by_data Object Details of the user who last modified the incident.
machine_generated Boolean Shows if the incident is machine generated or not.
closed_by_data Object Details of used who closed the incident.
created String Incident creation date and time.
modified String Last updated date and time of the incident.
opened_on String Date and time of when the incident was moved to open state.
opened_by_data Object Details of the user who moved the incident to the open state.
closed_on String Date and time when the incident was closed.
If incident is not closed, value of this param will be Null.
incident_date String Date and time of the incident creation.
detection_date String Date and time of when the incident was detected as malicious.
is_protected Boolean Shows if the incident is protected or not.
is_removed Boolean Shows if the incident is in the deleted state or not.
assigned_to String user_id of the assigned user.
assigned_to_data Object Details of the assigned user.
assigned_group String group_comm_id of the assigned user group.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group.
assignment_sla String Assignment SLA details of the incident.

It has two keys:

1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).

2. data: It has two keys:

- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.

- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
resolution_sla String Resolution SLA details of the incident.

It has two keys:

1. color: Associated color code(according to SLA breach level).

2. data: It has two keys:

- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.

- elapsed_time: Time elapsed between incident opening and SLA completion.
notification_sla List of Objects Details of the configured incident notifications (If enabled).
total_cost Integer Total cost incurred due to the incident.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows if the incident is bookmarked or not.
permanently_closed Boolean Shows if the incident is permanently closed or not.
resolution_due_date String Resolution SLA breach date of the incident.
can_update_instance Boolean Shows whether the instance can be updated by the user who requested it or not.
can_close_instance Boolean Shows if the user who requested it can close the incident or not.
is_paused Boolean Shows if the incident is in the paused state or not.
paused_by String user_id of the user who paused the incident.
paused_by_data Object Details of the user who paused the incident.
schema String Unique ID of the Incident Workflow that is being used by the incident.
schema_data Object Details of the Incident Workflow that is being used by the incident.
sources Array List of the sources for the incident.
sources_data Array of Objects Details of the sources for the incident.
labels Array List of the labels that are added to the incident.
labels_data Array of Objects Details of the labels that are added to the incident.
tactic_technique_pair Array List of the tactics and techniques used by the incident.
tactic_technique_pair_data Array of Objects Details of the tactics and techniques used by the incident.
business_units_impacted_data Array of Objects List of business units that are impacted by the incident.
locations_impacted_data Array of Objects List of locations that are impacted by the incident.

endpoints.name: Advanced Connect Modules
endpoints.description:
This API allows linking between components or custom modules within the platform. You can either append new components or update existing ones.

Request Parameters

Parameter Type Value
append Dict Enter the Dict containing link_from and link_to of components and their UUIDs
update Dict Enter the Dict containing link_from and link_to of components and their UUIDs

Note: append and update are mutually exclusive. Endpoint expects at least one among them to be present in the payload

Append and Update Request Parameters

Parameter Type Mandatory Value
link_from Dict Required Enter the component_identifier as key and UUID as value for the component for which you want to connect the dots.
Note: link_from accepts only a single component identifier key.
link_to List Required Enter a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary has a component_type as the key and a list of UUIDs as the value for the components to which the connection should be established.
Note: link_to can contain multiple component component_type.

Update - Request Parameters

Some links are not supported in append and are allowed only in update, they are:

Link from Component Identifier Link to Component Type
action incident
application general-user-manager, general-user-owner
device general-user-manager, general-user-owner

Note:

  • In update, you can connect to only one target component of each type at a time, while in append, you can connect to multiple.

  • component_type defines the “type” of the target component being connected.

Allowed Component Links

The following table lists valid mappings between components and the component types they can link to.

Link from Component Identifier Link to Component Type
incident action, application, asset-software, campaign, device, enhancement, general-user, knowledge-base, malware, pir, related_incident, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, ioc_-(IOC Types of IOCs), module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
campaign action, enhancement, incident, malware, pir, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
enhancement application, campaign, incident, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
vulnerability action, application, asset-software, campaign, device, enhancement, incident, malware, pir, threat-actor, threat-briefing, ioc_-(IOC Types of IOCs), module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
threat-actor action, application, asset-software, campaign, device, enhancement, incident, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, ioc_-(IOC Types of IOCs), module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
malware action, application, asset-software, campaign, device, enhancement, incident, pir, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, ioc_-(IOC Types of IOCs), module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
threat-briefing action, application, asset-software, campaign, device, enhancement, general-user, incident, malware, pir, threat-actor, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
knowledge-base action, incident
action application, asset-software, campaign, device, general-user, incident, knowledge-base, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
pir campaign, incident, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
application action, asset-software, device, general-user-manager, general-user-owner, incident, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
asset-software application, device, incident, enhancement, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)
endpoint action, application, asset-software, general-user-manager, general-user-owner, incident, malware, threat-actor, threat-briefing, vulnerability, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)

module-.* incident, campaign, enhancement, vulnerability, threat-actor, malware, threat-briefing, action, pir, application, asset-software, endpoint, general-user, module-(Component Identifier of Custom Modules)

Note:

  • To retrieve the component identifier of a custom module, you can use the List Custom Modules endpoint.

  • To retrieve the IOC type, you can use the Get List of Threat Intel Types.

endpoints.name: Get List of Actions
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the list of all actions from the CFTR application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/action/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any request parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Total number of Actions in CFTR application as per the query parameters.
results List of Objects Details of the Actions.
Each object provides details of one Action.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameters Type Description
title String Returns the title of the action.
unique_id String Returns the unique ID of the action.
created String Created date of the action in EPOCH time format.
modified String Last modified date of the action in EPOCH time format.
description String Description the an action.
assigned_to String User_id of the assigned user.
assigned_to_data Object Details of the assigned user.
assigned_group String Group_comm_id of the assigned user group.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group. Details include:
group_comm_id and group_name of the user group.
status String Status of the action. For example, open.
readable_id String Readable ID of the action. For example, ACT379.
created_by_data Object Details of the user who created the action. Details include:
username, email ,first name, last name, and so on.
can_update_instance Boolean Shows whether the instance can be updated by the user who requested it or not.
is_bookmarked Boolean True: Action is bookmarked.
False: Action is not bookmarked.
closed_by_data Object Details of the user who closed the action. Details include:
username, email ,first name, last name, and so on.
closed_on String Closure date of the action in EPOCH time format.
resolved_on String Resolved date of the action in EPOCH time format.
assignment_sla String Details of assignment SLA details of the action.
This parameter has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code (according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: time elapsed between action opening and SLA completion.
resolution_sla String Details of resolution SLA of the action.
This parameter has two keys:
1. color: Associated color code (according to SLA breach level).
2. data: It has two keys:
- sla_duration: SLA Breach time.
- elapsed_time: time elapsed between action opening and SLA completion.
resolution_due_date String Resolution due date of the action.
sla_stopped_on String Date and time at which the SLA stopped for the action.
type String Type of the action. For example, Recovery.
priority String Priority level of the action
type_data Object Details of the type of the action. Details include: unique_id, option_name, is_active, and so on.
priority_data Object Details of the priority level of the action.
labels List of Strings Unique IDs of the list of labels added to the action.
labels_data Object Details of the labels added to the action. Details include:
unique_id, title, color code, and so on.
created_from_template Boolean Displays if the action is created using a template or not.

previous and next

next shows the API endpoint to the next page.

request_full_path string Returns the full URL of the request including scheme, host, path, and query string.

Parameter Type Description

previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Total number of custom modules in CFTR application according to the filters applied.
results List of Objects Details of the custom modules.
Each object provides details of one incident.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter Type Description
component_identifier String Component identifier of a custom module. Example, MOD.
module_name String Name of the custom module.
icon String The icon identifier that is being used for the custom module.
unique_id String Unique ID of the custom module.
is_removable Boolean Shows whether the custom module can be deleted or not.

endpoints.name: Get List of Threat Briefings
endpoints.description:
Retrieve a list of Threat Briefings with details from the CFTR Application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/threat-briefing/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next key shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer The total number of Threat Briefings returned as per the entered query parameters.
results List of Objects Details of the Threat Briefings.
Each object provides the details of one Threat Briefing.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the Threat Briefing.
readable_id String Readable ID of the Threat Briefing.
title String Title of the Threat Briefing.
status String Current status of the Threat Briefing.
Allowed values:
- ACTIVE
- INACTIVE
created String Created date and time of the Threat Briefing.
modified String Last updated date and time of the Threat Briefing.
title_display String Title of the Threat Briefing.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows whether the Threat Briefing is bookmarked or not.
labels List List of unique_id of the attached labels.
labels_data List of Objects Details of the attached labels.
locations_data List of Objects Details of the locations linked to the threat briefing.
business_units_data List of Objects Details of the business units linked to the threat briefing.
created_by String Unique ID of the user who created the threat briefing.
created_by_data Object Details of the user who created the threat briefing.

endpoints.name: Get Details of a Threat Briefing
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of a specefic Threat Briefing from the CFTR application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/threat-briefing/:threat_briefing_unique_id/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the Threat Briefing.
readable_id String Readable ID of the Threat Briefing.
title String Title of the Threat Briefing.
description Text Description of the threat briefing.
status String Current status of the Threat Briefing.
Allowed values:
- ACTIVE
- INACTIVE
created String Created date and time of the Threat Briefing.
modified String Last updated date and time of the Threat Briefing.
title_display String Title of the Threat Briefing.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows whether the Threat Briefing is bookmarked or not.
labels List List of unique_id of the attached labels.
labels_data List of Objects Details of the attached labels.
locations_data List of Objects Details of the locations linked to the Threat Briefing.
business_units_data List of Objects Details of the business units linked to the Threat Briefing.
created_by String Unique ID of the user who created the Threat Briefing.
created_by_data Object Details of the user who created the Threat Briefing.

Response Parameters | Connect The Dots

Following are the response parameters corresponding the Connect The Dots section of the Threat Briefing. The parameters ending with _data contain the meta information for each connected component. The non _data parameters include an array of unique IDs of the connected components.

Starting from Respond v3.4.9, Connect the Dots will include the details of custom modules connected to the threat briefing.

Parameter Type Description
applications Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected applications.
applications_data Array of Objects Details of the connected applications.
softwares Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected software.
softwares_data Array of Objects Details of the connected software.
users Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected users.
users_data Array of Objects Details of the connected users.
endpoints Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected devices.
endpoints_data Array of Objects Details of the connected devices.
vulnerabilities Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_data Array of Objects Details of the connected vulnerabilities.
campaigns Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected campaigns.
campaigns_data Array of Objects Details of the connected campaigns.
malwares Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected malware.
malwares_data Array of Objects Details of the connected malware.
threat_actors Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat actors.
threat_actors_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat actors.
incidents Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected incidents.
incidents_data Array of Objects Details of the connected incidents.

Response Parameters | Custom Form Fields

In addition to the above mentioned parameters, the response parameters may vary as per the form configuration defined by your CFTR admin for Threat Briefings. For such parameters, the field_readable_key of each parameter is returned in the response. To retrieve the field_readable_key and additional metadata of a parameter, use the Form Tab Structure API for Threat Briefings.

Example

The following endpoint retrieves the field_readable_key for all custom fields in the Threat Briefing component:

{{base_url}}/cftrapi/openapi/v1/forms/fields/?object_identifier=threat-briefing

Following are some of the sample custom fields for Threat Briefing:

Parameter Type Required
privileges_required String Optional
additional_comments Text Optional

Response Parameters | Attachments

Parameter Type Description
attachments_data Array of Objects Details of each attachment of the Threat Briefing.

Response Parameters | Actions

Parameter Type Description
actions_data Array of Objects Details of the actions that are added for the Threat Briefing.

Response Parameters | Enhancements

Parameter Type Description
enhancements Array of UUID Strings List of the enhancements that are added for the Threat Briefing.
enhancements_data Array of Objects Details of the enhancements that are added for the Threat Briefing.

Response Parameters | PIRs

Parameter Type Description
pirs_data Array of Objects Details of the PIRs that are added for the Threat Briefing.

endpoints.name: Get List of Enhancements
endpoints.description:
Retrieve a list of all the enhancements with details from the CFTR application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/enhancement/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Total number of enhancements in the CFTR application as per the filters applied.
results List of Objects Details of the enhancements.
Each object provides details of one enhancement.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the enhancement in UUID-4 format.
readable_id String Unique readable ID of the enhancement. It starts with ENH followed by a unique number.
Example: ENH101
created String Enhancement creation date and time.
description Text Description of the enhancement.
modified String Last updated date and time of the enhancement.
title Text Title of the enhancement.
status String Current status of the enhancement.
Allowed values:
- open
- closed
priority String Priority level of the enhancement.
priority_data Object Details of the priority assigned. Details include:
unique_id,
option_name, and so on.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows if the enhancement is bookmarked or not.
modified_by_data Object Details of the user who last updated the enhancement. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
assigned_group String Unique ID of the assigned user group of the enhancement in UUID-4 format.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group. Details include: group name and group ID.
created_by_data Object Details of user who created the enhancement. Details include
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
assigned_to String Unique ID of the assigned user of the enhancement in UUID-4 format.
assigned_to_data Object Details of the assigned user. Details include
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
labels List of Strings List of Unique IDs of the labels associated with the enhancement in UUID-4 format.
labels_data List of Objects Details of labels added to the enhancement. Details include
title, unique_id, color_code, and so on.
enhancement_type List of Strings Option name of the enhancement types associated with the enhancement.
enhancement_type_data List of Objects Details of the enhancement types associated with the enhancement.

endpoints.description:
Update the details of an enhancement in the CFTR application using the values of assigned groups, labels, and the email IDs of assigned users.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

description String Optional Enter a description that best describes the key details of the enhancement.
status String Optional Enter the status of the enhancement.
Allowed values:
- open
- closed

Example:
"closed"

Default value: "open"
enhancement_type String Optional Enter the enhancement type.
Some of the examples of Enhancement types are:
• Process Update
• Strategy Change
• Policy Change

Example:
“Policy Change”
due_date Datetime Optional Enter the due date of the enhancement.
labels List Optional Enter the list of names of the labels to be attached to the enhancement. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of Labels: /openapi/v1/utils/label/
priority String Optional Enter the priority level of the
enhancement.

Levels are:
• Very High
• High
• Medium
• Low
• Very Low

Example:
“Very Low”
assigned_group String Optional Enter the name of the user group to assign the enhancement. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of

/openapi/v1/restauth/permission/group/
handoff_note Object

String		 Mandatory (If Assigned
Group or Assigned

handoff_note:

endpoints.name: Get Details of a Campaign
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of a campaign.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/campaign/:campaign_unique_id/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the campaign in UUID-4 format.
readable_id String Unique readable ID of the campaign. It starts with CMP followed by a unique number.
Example: CMP101
created String Campaign creation date and time.
description Text Description of the campaign.
modified String Last updated date and time of the campaign.
title String Title of the campaign.
title_display String Title of the campaign.
status String Current status of the campaign.
Allowed values:
ACTIVE
INACTIVE
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows if the campaign is bookmarked or not.
created_by_data Object Details of the user who created the campaign. Details include:
username, email ,first_name, last_name, and so on.
labels List of Strings Unique ID of the labels associated with the campaign in UUID-4 format.
labels_data List of Objects Details of labels added to the campaign. Details include:
title, unique_id, color_code, and so on.

Response Parameters | Connect The Dots

Following are the response parameters corresponding to the Connect The Dots section of the campaign. The parameters ending with _data contain the meta information for each connected component. The non __data_ parameters just include an array of unique_id referencing to connected components.

Starting from Respond v3.4.9, Connect the Dots will include the details of custom modules connected to the campaign.

Parameter Type Description
briefings Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat briefings.
briefings_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat briefings.
incidents Array UID Strings List of unique_id of the connected incidents.
incidents_data Array of Objects Details of the connected incidents.
malwares Array UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected malware.
malwares_data Array of Objects Details of the connected malware.
threat_actors Array UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat actors.
threat_actors_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat actors.
vulnerabilities Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_data Array of Objects Details of the connected vulnerabilities.

Response Parameters | Actions

Parameter Type Description
actions_data Array of Objects Details of the actions that are added to the campaign.

Response Parameters | PIRs

Parameter Type Description
pirs_data Array of Objects Details of the PIRs that are added to the campaign.

Response Parameters | Enhancements

Parameter Type Description
enhancements_data Array of Objects Details of the enhancements that are added to the campaign.

Response Parameters | Custom Fields

As CFTR form structure is dynamic and configurable, the response parameters might vary. The following table describes some examples of the custom fields:

Parameter Type
custom_campaign_field String
campaign_learning String
recovery_details String

Response Parameters | System Form Fields

Few of the fields or parameters have the values in UUID-4 format. These fields do not intake Option Name in the request as they are used internally for various additional responsibilities around Analytics, Relationships, and Filtering. These fields also include the parameters under Connect the Dots and Labels.

The fields include:

  1. All Connect the Dots params: You can retrieve the corresponding UUID-4 from the details page browser URL of the instance.

  2. Labels: You can retrieve the corresponding UUID-4 from Admin > Settings > Labels section.

endpoints.name: List Software
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of a list of software assets in the CFTR application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/asset-software/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next key shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer The total number of software returned as per the entered query parameters.
results List of Objects Details of the softwares.
Each object provides the details of one software.

Response Parameters | Results Object

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the software.
created String Created date and time of the software.
modified String Last updated date and time of the software.
title String Name of the software.
readable_id String Readable ID of the software.
labels List List of the labels that are added to the software.
labels_data List of Objects Details of labels added to the software. The details include:
title, unique_id, color_code, and so on.
software_status String Status of the sofware. For example, active.

endpoints.name: Get Software Details
endpoints.description:
Retrieve the details of a sofware in the CFTR application.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/asset-software/:software_unique_id/?

Request Parameters

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Response Parameters

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the software.
created String Software creation date and time.
modified String Software last updated date and time.
title String Name of the software.
software_id String ID of the software.
software_type List Type of the software. For example, Development Software.
title_display String Name of software.
readable_id String Readable ID of software. For example, SFT115.
software_status String Current status of the software.
purchase_date String Purchase date of the software.
created_by String user_id of the user who created the software.
created_by_data Object Details of user who added the software.
labels List List of unique_id labels that are added to the software.
labels_data List of Objects Details of the labels that are added to the software.
business_units_data List of Objects Details of business units that are impacted by the software
locations_data List of Objects Details of locations that are impacted by the software.
software_type_data Object Details of the software type.

Response Parameters | Connect The Dots

Following are the response parameters corresponding to the Connect The Dots section of the software. The parameters ending with _data include the meta information for each connected component. The non _data parameters include an array of unique IDs referencing to the connected components.

Starting from Respond v3.4.9, Connect the Dots will include the details of custom modules connected to the software.

Parameter Type Description
incidents Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected incidents.
incidents_data Array of Objects Details of the connected incidents.
briefings Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat briefings.
briefings_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat briefings.
threat_actors Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat actors.
threat_actors_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat actors.
vulnerabilities Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected connected vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_data Array of Objects Details of the connected vulnerabilities .
malwares Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected connected malwares.
malwares_data Array of Objects Details of the connected malwares .
endpoints Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected connected devices.
endpoint_data Array of Objects Details of the connected devices.

Response Parameters | Custom Fields

For such parameters, the field_readable_key of each parameter is returned in the response. To retrieve the field_readable_key and additional metadata of a parameter, use the Form Tab Structure API for software.

This API endpoint does not require any input parameter.

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter has two keys:
previous and next.
previous key shows the API endpoint to the previous page.
next key shows the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer The total number of PIRs returned as per the entered query parameters.
results List of Objects Details of the PIRs.
Each object provides the details of one PIR.

Parameter Type Description
unique_id String Unique ID of the PIR in UUID-4 format.
readable_id String Readable ID of the PIR.

- open
- closed

modified String Last updated date and time of the PIR.

labels List List of unique_id of the attached labels.

- Very Low

endpoints.name: Update PIR Using Field Values
endpoints.description:
Update the details of a PIR in the CFTR application using the values of assigned groups, labels, and the email IDs of assigned users.

Note: Starting from Respond v3.4.8 onwards, the following v2 endpoint is introduced to optimize performance:

v2/pir/:pir_unique_id/?

Request Parameters

Note: The default value of all the optional parameters is None, if the default value is not mentioned.

Parameter Type Required Description
title String Mandatory Enter a title for the PIR.
description Text Optional Enter a description for the PIR.
status String Optional Enter the current status of the PIR.
Allowed values:
open
closedDefault value:
open
is_bookmarked Boolean Optional Mention whether the PIR is bookmarked or not.
labels List of String Optional Enter the list of names of the labels to be attached to the PIR. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of Labels: /openapi/v1/utils/label/
priority String Mandatory Enter the priority level of the PIR.
Allowed values:
- Very Low
- Low
- Medium
- High
- Very High
assigned_to List of Strings Optional Enter the list of email IDs of the users to assign the PIR. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of
User:/openapi/v1/rest-auth/user/
assigned_group String Mandatory Enter the name of the user group to assign the PIR. You can use the following API endpoint to retrieve the list of
User Groups:
/openapi/v1/restauth/permission/group/
Request Parameters | Custom Form Fields

In addition to the above-mentioned parameters, the request parameters might vary as per the form configuration defined by your CFTR admin for PIRs. For such parameters, use the field_readable_key of each parameter. To retrieve the field_readable_key and additional metadata of a parameter, use the Form Tab Structure API for PIRs.

Example

The following endpoint retrieves the field_readable_key for all custom fields in the PIR component:

{{base_url}}/cftrapi/openapi/v1/forms/fields/?object_identifier=pir

Following are some of the sample custom fields for PIRs:

Parameter Type Required
privileges_required String Optional
additional_comments Text Optional

Response Parameters

Response Parameters | Regulatory Fields

Parameter Type Description
title String Title of the PIR.
unique_id String Unique ID of the PIR in UUID-4 format.
readable_id String Readable ID of the PIR.
description Text Description of the PIR.
created String Creation date and time of the PIR in ISO format.
modified String Last updated date and time of the PIR in ISO format.
status String Current status of the PIR.
Allowed values:
open
closed
created_by_data Object Details of user who created the PIR.
closed_by String user_id of the user who closed the PIR.
closed_by_data Object Details of user who closed the PIR.
closed_on String Closing date and time of the PIR in ISO format.
is_bookmarked Boolean Shows whether the PIR is bookmarked or not.
labels List of String List of unique_id of the attached labels.
labels_data List of Objects Details of the attached labels.
priority String Priority level of the PIR.
Allowed values:
- Very Low
- Low
- Medium
- High
- Very High
priority_data Object Details of the priority of the PIR.
assigned_to List of Stings List of Unique IDs of the assigned users in UUID-4 format.
assigned_to_data List of Objects Details on the list of assigned users of the PIR. Details include:
username, email, first_name, last_name, and so on.
assigned_group String Unique ID of the assigned user group in UUID-4 format.
assigned_group_data Object Details of the assigned user group. Details include:
group name and group ID

Response Parameters | Connect The Dots

Following are the response parameters corresponding the Connect The Dots section of PIR. The parameters ending with _data contain the meta information for each connected component. The non _data parameters include an array of unique IDs of the connected components.

Parameter Type Description
briefings Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat briefings.
briefings_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat briefings.
campaigns Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected campaigns.
campaigns_data Array of Objects Details of the connected campaigns.
malwares Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected malware.
malwares_data Array of Objects Details of the connected malware.
threat_actors Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected threat actors.
threat_actors_data Array of Objects Details of the connected threat actors.
incidents Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected incidents.
incidents_data Array of Objects Details of the connected incidents.
vulnerabilities Array of UUID Strings List of unique_id of the connected vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_data Array of Objects Details of the connected vulnerabilities.

Response Parameters | Custom Form Fields

As CFTR form structure is dynamic and configurable, the response parameters might vary. The following table describes some examples of the custom fields:

Parameter Type Required
privileges_required String Optional
additional_comments Text Optional

results Array of Objects Details of the Knowledge Base article.

endpoints.name: Advanced Search for Modules
endpoints.description:
Retrieves a list of entries of a module based on the query parameters and the parameters provided in the payload.

Request Parameters

Parameters Type Required Description
advanced_search_payload JSON Mandatory Pass the readable key of parameters and the respective values in key-value pairs to search entries.
advanced_search_payload:operator String Optional Pass the logical operator to apply to the passed parameters.
Allowed values:
- AND: Returns the entries that match all the parameter values passed.
- OR: Returns the entries that match at least one of the parameter values passed.
Default: AND
advanced_search_payload:operator_search_type

Note: This parameter is supported starting in Respond v3.4.9 onwards.		 String Optional Pass the matching logic for the search.
Allowed values:
exact_match: Returns results that exactly match the input value.
fuzzy_match: Returns results that are similar to the input value, including close matches or minor variations.

Response Parameters

Parameter Type Description
link Object This parameter includes two keys:
previous and next.
previous key returns the API endpoint to the previous page.
next key returns the API endpoint to the next page.
count Integer Returns the total number of module entries in the application base on the parameters passed in the query and payload.
results List of Objects Returns a list of module entries with details.
